name: Soroban Dojo: Abacus Mind
subtitle: Train the abacus, rank by rank
shortDescription: A 3D soroban and suanpan with twenty lessons, fifteen ranks from 10 kyu to 5 dan, flash anzan and a rival race.
longDescription:
The soroban reached Japan from the Chinese suanpan in the sixteenth century and became the tool of shopkeepers and bank clerks, and later of champions who can add a column of numbers in their heads by picturing the beads. Soroban Dojo is a training hall for both instruments.

A 3D abacus of lacquered beads on a rosewood frame sits in front of you. Drag a bead to the beam to count it, away to release it, and hear the click.

Twenty lessons run from the first bead to long division, each with a short teaching card and problems worked one number at a time, checked after every number. Hint points at the bead to move and explains the rule: direct moves, the heaven bead, five-friends, ten-friends and carrying, taking away and borrowing, multiplication by partial products, and division by successive subtraction.

Walk the Dojo path through fifteen ranks, from 10 kyu to 5 dan. Each examination is ten problems on a list, answered on the abacus; seven right passes and nine or ten earns the third star, with longer, wider and faster problems at each rank.

Auto Play lets the computer work a problem and say why it moves each bead; pause, change speed, press Think, or take over. Flash Anzan flashes numbers that vanish so you can set their total on the abacus. Sixty-second drills come in eight levels, a rival race pits you against a trained opponent, and a daily set keeps a streak. Choose soroban or suanpan, with 5 to 13 rods.

Free with ads. Go ad-free with a monthly pass or by earning time from videos.
monetization: Free with ads, optional monthly ad-free
